Random-Effects Mixture Meta-Analysis

remix.Rd

Fits finite mixture models for random-effects meta-analysis using maximum likelihood estimation in OpenMx. Each mixture class has its own mean effect size and residual heterogeneity variance. Note that OpenMx must be loaded using library(OpenMx) before calling this function.

Usage

remix(
  yi,
  vi,
  classes = 2L,
  mu = c("varying", "equal"),
  tau2 = c("varying", "equal"),
  run = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

yi

Numeric vector of observed effect sizes.

vi

Numeric vector of known sampling variances.

classes

Integer vector specifying the number of mixture classes to fit. Defaults to 1L:2L.

mu

Whether component means are varying or equal.

tau2

Whether component heterogeneity variances are varying or equal.

run

Logical. If TRUE (the default), the model is estimated using OpenMx. If FALSE, the unestimated OpenMx model object is returned, allowing further modification before estimation.

...

Arguments passed to other functions.

Value

A fitted model object, or a "mixture_list" when multiple class counts are specified.

Details

The estimation procedure is described in Van Lissa, Garnier-Villarreal, & Anadria (2023): starting values are determined by way of K-means clustering, then the model is estimated using simulated annealing, followed by maximum likelihood optimization.

References

Van Lissa, C. J., Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Anadria, D. (2023). Recommended Practices in Latent Class Analysis using the Open-Source R-Package tidySEM. Structural Equation Modeling. doi:10.1080/10705511.2023.2250920

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(7894)
df <- sim_remix_fixed_tau()

# Conventional random-effects meta-analysis
res1 <- remix(df$yi, df$vi, classes = 1)
if(requireNamespace("metafor")){
  res_mf <- metafor::rma(yi = df$yi, vi = df$vi)
  res_mf$b[1,1] - res1$M$values[1, 1]
  res_mf$tau2 - res1$S$values[1, 1]
}

# Two-class random-effects mixture model
res2 <- remix(df$yi, df$vi, classes = 2)
table_fit(res2)
table_results(res2)
} # }
